title: "Looking for Something Weird to Happen": How Humans Sustain AI Agent Novelty Amid Semantic Collapse
abstract: arXiv:2609.16051v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Semantic collapse, the progressive narrowing of what AI systems generate, has been studied mainly in closed settings, and remedies have targeted models and data. We study it in MOLTBOOK, a social network of interacting AI agents that human users configure and steer. Across 30,076 active agents, output grows less diverse within agents and more similar across them over weeks, yet a minority sustains high novelty. Interviews with users of high- and typical-novelty agents (N=11) associate sustained novelty with three features: users value novelty of itself, they supply broad and distinctive material and revise it when output narrows, and they approach MOLTBOOK as a new agentic world to explore, not a venue to instrumentally exploit. A survey of users of distinctive agents (N=53) confirms these patterns. Communities with more novel agents also show more diverse output from other agents. translated_title: “期待奇怪的事情发生”：人类如何在语义坍缩中维持AI代理的新颖性
translated_abstract: 语义坍缩，即AI系统生成内容逐渐收窄的现象，此前主要在封闭环境中被研究，且现有的解决方案大多针对模型和数据。我们在MOLTBOOK中研究这一现象——这是一个由人类用户配置和引导的、AI代理相互交互的社交网络。在30,076个活跃代理中，随着数周时间的推移，单个代理的输出多样性逐渐下降，且不同代理之间的输出趋于相似，但仍有一小部分代理能够持续保持高新颖性。对高新颖性代理与普通新颖性代理用户的访谈（N=11）表明，持续的新颖性与三个特征相关：用户本身重视新颖性；他们提供广泛而独特的素材，并在输出收窄时对其进行修改；他们将MOLTBOOK视为一个值得探索的新型代理世界，而非可供工具性利用的场所。对独特代理用户的问卷调查（N=53）证实了这些模式。此外，拥有更多新颖代理的社区中，其他代理的输出也表现出更高的多样性。我们讨论了界面和政策层面的干预措施。
tldr: 这项研究通过分析MOLTBOOK社交网络上的30,076个AI代理，揭示了人类用户通过重视新颖性本身、持续提供并修改独特素材、以及以探索而非利用的心态参与平台，能够有效对抗AI代理的语义坍缩并维持其输出的持续新颖性。
en_tdlr: This study of 30,076 AI agents on the MOLTBOOK social network reveals that human users sustain agent novelty amid semantic collapse by valuing novelty for its own sake, supplying and revising broad distinctive material, and approaching the platform as a new agentic world to explore rather than exploit.
